title: Tech Note: 4D Connects with Wireless Markup Language

historical_commentary.text: This note reflects the WAP/WML mobile-web hype of 2000-2001, showing how 4D's web server could dynamically generate Wireless Markup Language content for the WAP-enabled feature phones of that era. WAP and WML were almost entirely abandoned within a few years in favor of standard mobile HTML/CSS/JS as smartphones matured, making this note purely of historical interest as a snapshot of an early, ultimately unsuccessful mobile-web technology bet, with essentially no direct technical relevance to modern mobile web or app development via 4D.
related_updates: WAP and WML were abandoned industry-wide within a few years in favor of standard mobile HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and later native mobile apps
Modern 4D mobile/web development uses standard responsive web technologies or native app frameworks (e.g., via 4D's Qodly/web project tooling) rather than WML
